description: The overlay's name postings now hold each segment's canonical rows instead of its raw ones -- the same intersection step5_build_kind_postings has always applied to the kind postings. Five readers take those postings, and this suite pins what each of them answers, because the change is only safe if the rows it removes were rows no answer carried: the pattern tier and the name-equality tier propose candidates a residual WHERE then verifies, the scan collapses duplicates before delivering, the ascending name streams deliver posting entries as rows, and symbol resolution picks among them. The counted GROUP BY that this makes possible is pinned in open_defects beside the scan it has to agree with.

cases.name: a_name_equality_answers_the_rows_it_answered
cases.description: prefilter_global proposes lookup_name_bitmap's rows for a name equality and the row filter decides them. Dropping the intra-segment duplicates from that bitmap cannot move the answer, because the duplicates agree with a survivor on name, kind and line, which is the key the delivered rows are collapsed on. Pinned by the row, not only the count, so a bitmap that lost the wrong row fails here.

cases.name: the_pattern_tier_answers_what_it_answered
cases.description: prefilter_name_values unions the postings of every FST key the pattern accepts. The union is smaller now and still a superset of the answer, which is all a proposing tier has to be -- 1,201 rows match this pattern either way.
cases.fql: FIND symbols WHERE name LIKE '%segment%' LIMIT 3

cases.name: the_duplicates_the_postings_dropped_were_never_in_an_answer
cases.description: The file whose raw name postings carry 57 rows named '0' and whose canonical set carries 48. The scan reached 48 before the intersection and reaches 48 after it: the nine rows that left the postings are rows the dedupe pass had already been collapsing away. That is the whole safety argument for this change, on the corpus where the gap is known.
cases.fql: FIND symbols WHERE name = '0' IN 'crates/forgeql-core/src/transforms/diff.rs' LIMIT 60

cases.name: the_ascending_name_stream_fills_its_page
cases.description: A bare LIMIT rides stream_names_asc, which pushes one row per posting entry and stops once it holds the page. A duplicate entry used to consume one of those places and then merge into its survivor downstream, so the page could come back shorter than it asked for while `total` -- taken from the stored canonical counts -- counted neither of them. Rows and total are drawn from the same set now. 25 asked for, 25 delivered, out of the corpus's 59,636 canonical rows.

cases.name: resolution_reaches_the_node_it_reached
cases.description: Symbol resolution takes lookup_name_bitmap's rows and picks among them. step45_dedup_segments keeps the LOWEST row id of each (name, fql_kind, line) group, so the first candidate in any segment is the one that survives and resolution lands where it landed. What it can no longer reach is a strictly later row agreeing with that survivor on all three -- which is the anomaly, not the behaviour: those rows are one answer row, and a reader that resolved to the second of them was choosing by an accident of ordering.
